# Banded

> Banded (https://banded.fm) maps the real-world connections between musical artists: shared band members, side projects, collaborations, producers and opening acts. It is a single-page web app that runs in the browser; its pages need JavaScript, so this file describes them in plain text.

Banded is built from MusicBrainz data dumps (artists, band membership, recording and production credits), concert history from setlist.fm, and upcoming concerts from Pollstar. The graph is precomputed into a SQLite database that the browser downloads and queries locally. It is free, has no ads, and is open source.

## Pages

- [Home](https://banded.fm/): what Banded is, with a link to each page.
- [Graph](https://banded.fm/#/graph): search an artist and explore their network: band members, former members, supporting musicians, artists they played or sang with, producers and opening acts. Click a node to add its connections.
- [Map](https://banded.fm/#/map): the world's music scenes on a map: in each major city, clusters of connected artists, named by genre and era.
- [Proximity](https://banded.fm/#/proximity): enter artists you like and an artist to compare; Banded scores 0 to 100 how close they are, from the strongest path of relationships between them, and shows that path.
- [Upcoming](https://banded.fm/#/upcoming): enter a city, dates and artists you like; Banded lists upcoming concerts there, ranked by how close each headliner is to your artists.
- [Play](https://banded.fm/#/play): Six Degrees of Music, a daily puzzle: connect two artists in as few steps as you can, one connection at a time. Custom puzzles can be made and shared by link.
- [About](https://banded.fm/#/about): how it works and FAQs.

## Notes

- MusicBrainz and setlist.fm are crowd-sourced, so some artists, connections and shows are missing.
- Source code: https://github.com/banded-fm/banded
